supplementaryReferences.title: Edible tuber product and warm-season habitat
supplementaryReferences.note: The food product is a tuber, not a potato-family fruit. Warm summer-rainfall cultivation with little frost is described; winter/spring flowering after leaf loss is not a dated tuber-digging calendar.

supplementaryReferences.title: Tuber planting and harvest cycle
supplementaryReferences.doc: SANBI PlantZAfrica: Coleus esculentus, Harvesting and storage of tubers
supplementaryReferences.note: Tubers can be harvested 4–6 months after planting, depending on rainfall, soil and situation. Source planting context is the onset of early spring rains, late August–early September in South African summer-rainfall areas. This is a tuber planting cycle, not tree first-bearing age; it does not establish universal picking months. Shelf life is described as relatively short without a numeric duration.

care: Use loose, well-drained soil in full sun under suitably warm conditions.
Record tuber harvest by planting batch and bed area, rather than a generic fruit-tree maturity curve.
The SANBI tuber-cycle reference is 4–6 months after planting, dependent on water, soil and position. Record the actual planting date and mature tuber harvest.
purchase: Obtain correctly identified planting tubers or pieces. A local named selection and food kg/plant benchmark remain unverified.
